mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 0.15% per annum signals monetary easing, reducing discount rates for equity valuation and producing positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns due to improved risk appetite and lower cost of capital.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of instances where FEDFUNDS declines by at least 0.05 percentage points over the prior 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeding 5.0% in a 3-month window indicates deteriorating labor market conditions, triggering negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns through reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings growth expectations.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of instances where UNRATE exceeds 5.0% for at least 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent expansion in GDP (GDPC1) above $13,500 billion and industrial production (INDPRO) above 95.0 index level signals robust economic momentum, driving positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns via strengthened corporate earnings and investment demand.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of instances where both GDPC1 exceeds $13,500 billion and INDPRO exceeds 95.0.

mechanism_narrative: Monetary tightening conditions (FEDFUNDS > 0.10% and CPIAUCSL > 230.0) indicate rising inflation and interest rates, causing negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns through reduced liquidity and equity valuation compression.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of instances where FEDFUNDS exceeds 0.10% and CPIAUCSL exceeds 230.0.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in employment (PAYEMS) above 130,000 thousand persons consistently precedes positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns by signaling stronger consumer spending and corporate revenue growth in the economic cycle.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of instances where PAYEMS increases by at least 5,000 thousand persons over the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: A housing market contraction (HOUST < 700 thousand units) indicates weakening consumer demand and construction activity, triggering negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns through reduced economic growth signals.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of instances where HOUST falls below 700 thousand units.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO < 95.0) and housing starts (HOUST < 750 thousand units) signals broad-based economic contraction, producing negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns due to reduced manufacturing output and consumer demand.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of instances where both INDPRO and HOUST fall below their respective thresholds.

mechanism_narrative: Late-cycle labor market conditions (UNRATE < 4.5% and PAYEMS > 130,000 thousand persons) indicate peak economic activity, driving positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns through accelerated corporate earnings growth and investor confidence in sustained expansion.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of instances where UNRATE is below 4.5% and PAYEMS exceeds 130,000 thousand persons.
